notes: Waves are consistent and correct (parts 4 'Chaar barabar tukde', cut 1/3 'Teen barabar tukde', cut 1/4 'Ek chauthai', parts 3 'Ek tihai'). With marks false the child must judge equal size herself, so a child who cuts uneven pieces is graded off ('PAAS' / 'itna chook'), which shows the unequal-parts mix-up where it goes wrong. The subs state the rule ('Chaar tukde sab ek jaise hone chahiye') but not where to cut, so not counted as giving the answer. Minor, not counted: 'silisila' is a misspelling of 'silsila' and a literary word for class 4; wave 3's sub says 'Chaar tukde' though one cut at 1/4 makes two pieces. Both screens are legible with nothing cut off; the coach line 'Barabar tukde dekho' is low-contrast but readable.

There is one fraction per item on a single 0 to 1 line with 8 ticks (1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/3, 1/6), all of them correct positions. A child who thinks 1/8 > 1/4 would place 1/8 to the right of 1/4 and miss, so the mix-up is shown. No title or sub names a position or the rule ('Pizza line', 'Har item ko line par rakho', 'Ab apni jagah chuno'). Not counted: 1/3 and 1/6 do not fall on the eighths ticks, so the child has to estimate them. The 'WAVE 1/3' counter looks like a fraction on a fractions screen and might confuse a child. Many feedback strings are English ('landed', 'Run complete', 'SAME SPOT'), which is within Hinglish. Both screens are legible with nothing cut off.
